introduction: These hundred readings call truthfulness the foundation of all human virtues and trustworthiness the door of security for all who dwell on earth. They speak of parents and children, merchants and employees, editors, officials and governments, and many are brief counsels repeated to one person after another. Beside them stand the commandments and proverbs of other scriptures on honest weights, kept oaths and faithful stewards, with Confucius on the trust without which no state can stand. The harder cases are there too: Plato's royal lie and Machiavelli's advice to princes, Iago praising a good name, Jacob's disguise, Bacon on the pleasure of a small untruth, Mill on whether truth prevails, and Pilate's question. They ask what truthfulness costs and why it should be kept when it does not pay.
questions: The readings call truthfulness the foundation of all virtues. Which other virtue have you seen fail because honesty was missing underneath it?
Plato allows rulers one useful lie and Machiavelli tells princes to break faith when it suits them. What happens, in your observation, to institutions that act this way?
Proverbs says the wounds of a friend are faithful. How do you tell a truth that should be spoken from one that is only unkind?
Iago speaks eloquently of a good name. What distinguishes being trustworthy from appearing so, and how can others tell?
Jeremiah says the heart is deceitful above all things. Where are you most likely to deceive yourself, and what helps?
Confucius says a state cannot stand without the people's trust. What would rebuild trust where you live or work?

outside.why: Confucius said: I do not know how a man without truthfulness is to get on.
Proverbs says that the lip of truth shall be established for ever, but a lying tongue is but for a moment.
Proverbs says: train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

Plato's Socrates proposes one needful falsehood, a royal lie, to be told to the rulers and the rest of the city for their good. Is there ever a lie that those who teach or govern may tell for the sake of those in their care?
Leviticus commands: ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another.
Proverbs says that a false balance is abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is His delight.
Jesus said that he that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.
Jesus told his followers not to pray as the hypocrites do, who love to be seen of men.
The psalmist says to God: behold, Thou desirest truth in the inward parts.
The psalm asks who shall dwell in God's holy hill, and answers: he that walketh uprightly and speaketh the truth in his heart.
Jesus said: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay; whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
The Tao Te Ching says that sincere words are not fine, and fine words are not sincere. How are truthfulness and courtesy to be joined, when each can undo the other?
The Letter to the Ephesians says: putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour, for we are members one of another.
Proverbs says that faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful. When does kindness require a truth that hurts?
Milton, pleading for an unlicensed press, asked who ever knew Truth put to the worse in a free and open encounter.
John Stuart Mill called it a pleasant falsehood that truth always triumphs over persecution, one which all experience refutes. If truth does not win by itself, what must those who publish it do?
Urged to agree with the king's other prophets, Micaiah answered: what the Lord saith unto me, that will I speak.
Isaiah describes a people who say to their prophets: speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits. What part do listeners play in the lies they are told?
The Qur’an says: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away; falsehood is ever bound to vanish.
The Qur’an says: woe unto the defrauders, who demand full measure from others and give less when they measure for them.
The Qur’an says that God commands you to restore deposits to their owners.
The Book of Kings says of the men who paid the temple workmen that no reckoning was asked of them, for they dealt faithfully.
Proverbs says that confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
The psalmist laments: mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me. How is trust rebuilt after it has been betrayed?
Paul says that it is required in stewards that a man be found faithful.
In the parable the master says: well done, thou good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things.
Peter asked Ananias why he had kept back part of the price while pretending to give all: thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.
The Qur’an says that the trust was offered to the heavens, the earth and the hills, and they shrank from it, and man assumed it.
Daniel's rivals sought occasion against him and could find none, forasmuch as he was faithful.
John the Baptist told the tax collectors to exact no more than was appointed, and the soldiers to be content with their wages.
Jethro advised Moses to choose as rulers able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness.
Confucius said that a state can give up arms and even food, but if the people have no faith in their rulers there is no standing for the state.
Machiavelli advised that a wise lord cannot, nor ought he to, keep faith when such observance may be turned against him. What becomes of a country whose government acts on that advice?
The psalm praises the one that sweareth to his own hurt, and changeth not.
Madison wrote that if men were angels no government would be necessary, and so built checks on those who govern. Is confidence in others a risk to be taken, or a thing to be earned and verified?
Paul speaks of providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
Zechariah says: speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates.
Jesus said: when ye fast, be not as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance.
Huckleberry Finn tries to pray while playing double and concludes: you can't pray a lie.
The Qur’an asks the believers: why say ye that which ye do not?
Jesus told Pilate: to this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth.
Pilate answered Jesus with a question, what is truth, and went out. What is the difference between asking that question and waiting for an answer?
Jesus said: ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

Pascal mocked a justice bounded by a river: truth on this side of the Pyrenees, error on the other. If people in every land call their own belief the truth, how is truthfulness toward God to be recognized?
Balaam says in the Book of Numbers: God is not a man, that He should lie.
Exodus commands: thou shalt not raise a false report, nor join with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.
The Qur’an says: confound not truth with falsehood, nor knowingly conceal the truth.
Elijah asked the people on Carmel: how long halt ye between two opinions?
Paul says that charity rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth.
The first letter of John says: let us not love in word, neither in tongue, but in deed and in truth.
Proverbs says that a good name is rather to be chosen than great riches.
Shakespeare has it said that good name in man and woman is the immediate jewel of their souls.
The speaker of those lines is Iago, who has already said of himself: I am not what I am. How is a trustworthy person told from one who has only the reputation?
Proverbs says that the integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
The Qur’an praises those who are shepherds of their pledge and their covenant.
The Qur’an says: be careful of your duty to God, and be with the truthful.
The psalm says: keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.
The Letter to the Colossians says: lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds.
Francis Bacon admitted that a mixture of a lie doth ever add pleasure. Why are small untruths so attractive, and what do they cost?
The elder writes: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
The psalm says: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
Jeremiah told the exiles to seek the peace of the city where they were held, for in its peace they would have peace.
Zacchaeus stood and said: if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
Proverbs says that bread of deceit is sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
Jeremiah says that the prophets prophesy falsely, and my people love to have it so. Why is honest counsel so often given and so seldom taken?
Leviticus requires just balances, just weights and a just measure in every dealing.
The Qur’an says: keep the covenant; fill the measure when ye measure, and weigh with a right balance.
The Qur’an says: hide not testimony; he who hideth it, verily his heart is sinful.
Jeremiah says that the heart is deceitful above all things: who can know it? If the heart deceives even its owner, where does trustworthiness begin?
The psalm says that he shall stand in the holy place who hath clean hands and a pure heart, nor sworn deceitfully.
Paul lists the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.
James says: swear not; let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay.
The Dhammapada says: speak the truth, do not yield to anger; give, if thou art asked for little.
Proverbs says that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
Milton writes of the seraph Abdiel: faithful found among the faithless, faithful only he.
Polonius advises: to thine own self be true, and thou canst not then be false to any man. Is being true to oneself enough to make a person truthful to others?
Proverbs says that the just man walketh in his integrity, and his children are blessed after him.
The Qur’an says that whoever breaks his oath breaks it only to his own soul's hurt.
Paul asks Timothy to be an example in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Proverbs says that lying lips are abomination to the Lord, but they that deal truly are His delight.
The Qur’an names together the men who speak the truth and the women who speak the truth.
Kipling counts it a mark of maturity to bear to hear the truth you have spoken twisted by knaves to make a trap for fools.
The Qur’an says: be not like her who unravels the thread after she has made it strong, making your oaths a deceit between you.

Confucius said that he once heard people's words and gave them credit for their conduct, and now hears their words and looks at their conduct. How much should trust depend on what people say of themselves?
Jesus said: woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you, for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
Aristotle said that, while both are dear, piety requires us to honour truth above our friends.
In the parable a man going to a far country delivered his goods to his servants, to each according to his ability.
The Qur’an says: be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for God, even though it be against yourselves.
Emerson wrote that a friend is a person with whom I may be sincere; before him I may think aloud.

Wilfred Owen called the saying that it is sweet and fitting to die for one's country the old Lie, told to children ardent for glory. Which honoured sayings of your own society would not survive a truthful look?
Carlyle called his hero one of those who cannot but be in earnest, whom Nature herself has appointed to be sincere.
The psalmist says: he that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house.
Proverbs says that he that walketh uprightly walketh surely, but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
Confucius said that if names be not correct, language is not in accordance with the truth of things, and affairs cannot be carried on to success.
In John's Gospel Jesus prays: sanctify them through Thy truth; Thy word is truth.
The Qur’an says: guard your duty to God, and speak words straight to the point.
Jacob obtained his father's blessing by a disguise: the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. What do the scriptures teach by recording the deceits of those they honour?
The psalm calls blessed the one in whose spirit there is no guile.
John's Gospel says that every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light.
Jesus said: ye shall know them by their fruits; do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

luke-content-with-your-wages.text: Then came also publicans to be baptized, and said unto him, Master, what shall we do? And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you. luke-zacchaeus-fourfold.text: And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold

kings-micaiah-that-will-i-speak.text: And the messenger that was gone to call Micaiah spake unto him, saying, Behold now, the words of the prophets declare good unto the king with one mouth: let thy word, I pray thee, be like the word of one of them, and speak that which is good. And Micaiah said, As the Lord liveth, what the Lord saith unto me, that will I speak

isaiah-speak-unto-us-smooth-things.text: That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the Lord: Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits

genesis-jacob-deceives-isaac.text: And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not. And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau
